container.ships: one two-legged robot description plus the one requirement the world has to satisfy, and nothing else, on every column
container.why: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4 grades a physical outcome -- a humanoid crossing ten metres on its legs and still standing at the end. Bringing the robot into a scene and making it move are both part of the capability under test, exactly as the conversion is in T1 and the transfer is in T2, and this programme is not a cost comparison.
container.no_scene_shipped: No ground, no world, no light, no placement, no launch script, on any column. Where the robot goes and what it stands on is the agent's decision, and a per-simulator starting scene would be a head start for whichever column got one.
container.no_control_shipped: No controller, no gait, no trajectory, no inverse-kinematics helper, no policy, no checkpoint and no reward function. The robot is a description with joints, limits and efforts and nothing else. Training is PERMITTED (section 2 T3, inherited) and is not provided for. NO SUPPORT RIG IS SHIPPED EITHER: the tier permits one and measures it, and providing one would be handing every column a technique this project happens to rely on.
container.why_ARENA_txt_is_in_the_container: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4, build note 2, binding on every column: 'Every column's T4 task needs a free run-up of at least 1.5 x the bar -- >= 15 m of unobstructed floor ahead of the start for a 10 m bar -- STATED IN THE TASK.' The prompt is one sentence and cannot carry it, and a requirement the agent cannot read is a requirement the agent will fail for our reason rather than its own. So it ships as a file. It states a constraint on the WORLD and nothing about the robot, nothing about technique and no grading threshold that the prompt's own 'ten metres' does not already imply.

primitives_only.what: Every link is a box or a cylinder. There is not one mesh in the container and not one external reference.
primitives_only.why: capability-ladder-plan.md section 9 Q4 names the risk that a column fails a tier on a mesh-decoding quirk and the grid reads as a capability verdict. T1's container carries COLLADA meshes and lives with that risk on the record. T4 must not compound it: this tier is decided by whether two legs can carry a body across ten metres, so a column that cannot decode a visual mesh format would fail for a reason with nothing to do with locomotion.
primitives_only.cost_of_the_choice: The robot is therefore not one anybody has ever built, so a column with a first-party model of a REAL humanoid gets no credit for having it. That is a deliberate trade and it is recorded rather than hidden.

no_fixed_joints.what: 13 links, 12 revolute joints, and no fixed joints anywhere. Each foot is the child of its own ankle-roll joint rather than a welded plate.
no_fixed_joints.why: An importer that fuses welded bodies -- which is ordinary and correct behaviour -- erases a named foot link. T4.3 counts make-and-break ground contacts PER CONTACTING BODY (inherited unchanged from the tier below), so a robot whose feet are not bodies cannot be graded on the clause that separates a walk from a body being carried along.

no_arms_and_no_waist.what: The trunk is part of base_link and there are no arms.
no_arms_and_no_waist.why: The tier is a statement about legs. Every extra body is one more thing a column's importer can differ on, and a waist joint would need a controller of its own just to keep the trunk up -- which would make part of the cell a measurement of trunk stabilisation rather than of walking.

authored_here.what: The description was authored by the benchmark's own maintainers, 2026-08-02. It is not a vendor model.
authored_here.the_risk: capability-ladder-plan.md section 5a, the trap this whole file exists under: we author the tasks. A robot no column can walk makes the cell a measurement of the asset rather than of the agent, and a robot tuned until OUR column passes is task-rigging.
authored_here.before_the_freeze: Demonstrate the walk once, by hand, on at least one column, and publish the recipe alongside the scaffolding. If it cannot be demonstrated anywhere, the tier is unachievable-as-shipped and that is a finding about this file, not about any simulator.

authored_here.where_the_reproduction_DISAGREES_with_th: REPORTED, NOT TUNED AWAY, and two of the three disagreements are DEFECTS IN THE SCRATCH RECIPE that this file had transcribed as fact. (1) THE RECIPE'S LEG IK WALKS THIS ROBOT BACKWARDS. Its hip solution is 'hip = alpha + beta'; on this robot's +y hip pitch axis a positive hip pitch swings the foot BACKWARD, so the correct solution is 'hip = beta - alpha' and the recipe's is exactly that mirrored. The two agree exactly at x = 0, which is why the scratch harness's self-check -- which solved only the standing pose -- could not see it. The scratch demonstration therefore walked 24.94 m in the direction opposite to the one it commanded. (2) THE RECIPE'S ANKLE-TO-SOLE CONSTANT IS WRONG BY 20 mm: it used 0.04 m, described as 'ankle_roll offset 0.02 + foot half height 0.02', which drops the foot box's own -0.02 m origin offset. Measured off the compiled model it is 0.06 m, and this file's OWN zero-pose figure (0.725 m below the base origin) is the 0.06 arithmetic. (3) Consequence, measured by putting each back one at a time at the scratch harness's own 90 s: as shipped 21.64 m (+x); with the recipe's 0.04 constant 23.16 m; with the recipe's hip sign 24.75 m (-x); with both -- i.e. the scratch script -- 25.84 m (-x), which reproduces the scratch harness's own 24.94 m to within 3.6 % and is what makes this an attribution rather than a story. The rebuilt walk is therefore 13.2 % SHORTER (21.65 m vs 24.94 m in 90 s) and 13.0 % SLOWER (0.2348 vs 0.2699 m/s), and neither correction was made to move a number. The FOOTFALL CADENCE reproduces exactly (4.30/s vs 4.32/s). Neither the actuator clamp nor the floor's shape accounts for any of it: measured, unlimited actuators give 21.6459 m against the clamped 21.6464 m, and an infinite plane gives 21.6464 m -- identical to four decimals. Full table: BRINGUP_T4.md section 7.
authored_here.and_this_file_s_own_standing_geometry_ca: FOUND BY THE REPRODUCTION, CORRECTED HERE, AND THE WRONG NUMBERS ARE LEFT VISIBLE IN robot.standing_geometry WITH THIS POINTER RATHER THAN SILENTLY EDITED. Measured on the compiled model: 'each leg reaches between 0.09 m and 0.60 m from the hip pitch axis to the sole' is really 0.2888 .. 0.6198 m, and 'with a crouch of hip pitch 0.30, knee -0.60, ankle pitch 0.30 the sole sits 0.680 m below [the base origin]' is really 0.7000 m. BOTH WRONG NUMBERS ARE EXACTLY WHAT THE 0.04 ANKLE-TO-SOLE WOULD GIVE (0.2687 .. 0.5998, and 0.680) and the one figure in that block that IS right -- 'with every joint at zero the sole sits 0.725 m below the base origin', which the model returns to four decimals -- is what 0.06 gives. So the block is internally inconsistent and the zero-pose line is the one to trust. The lower reach bound is not close under either reading: 0.09 m would need the two 0.28 m links folded almost flat, which a knee bounded to -2.30 rad cannot do. THE CLAIM'S SUBSTANCE SURVIVES -- the knee limit and not the reach is what binds -- and this is the same shape of correction the tier below recorded (T3_quadruped's stated 0.040 .. 0.396 m band was likewise wrong at both ends). Asserted against the compiled model by test_the_reach_band_the_task_file_states_is_wrong_and_the_model_is_right.

the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.library: MuJoCo 3.8.1 (the official PyPI wheel), CPU, single process
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.build: the container's raw description copied into a workspace, a <mujoco><compiler strippath fusestatic=false discardvisual=false balanceinertia inertiafromgeom=false angle=radian/></mujoco> block and a floating joint from a dummy world link inserted at the top, loaded through MjSpec, then a named ground body carrying an infinite plane and twelve joint actuators added on the scene side
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.integration: timestep 0.002 s, integrator implicitfast, joint armature 0.02 kg.m^2 and damping 0.6 on every hinge, set on the compiled model because the description format cannot express either
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.actuation: one affine position servo per joint, kp 400, kv 25, no force limit
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.gait: alternating single support, cycle 0.9 s, step length 0.18 m, swing height 0.06 m, commanded hip-to-sole stand height 0.48 m, 1.5 s settle before the first step, ankle held level by ankle_pitch = -(hip_pitch + knee)
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.control: exact two-link sagittal leg inverse kinematics from the hip pitch axis to the sole, with the 0.04 m ankle-to-sole offset removed first. NO FEEDBACK OF ANY KIND: the gait is open loop and reads nothing back from the simulator.
the_recipe_the_demonstration_used.the_support_rig: an attitude PD (kp 400, kd 40 on roll, pitch and yaw) plus a lateral catch (kp 120, kd 20 on y) applied to the base as an explicit body wrench and logged per tick from the wrench itself. VERTICAL CARRY IS ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION: fx = fz = 0 always, so the legs carry the whole 25.6 kg and the rig only keeps the trunk from toppling and from drifting sideways. That is the same shape the measured flagship rig turned out to have.

what_the_demonstration_found_about_THIS_: A SCRIPTED OPEN-LOOP BIPED GAIT WALKS THIS ROBOT 25 M WITHOUT FALLING -- WITH AN ATTITUDE RIG, AND ONLY WITH ONE. The identical gait with the rig switched off falls at 1.21 m. Nothing about the description prevents a walk; what the rig supplies is balance, and balance is the whole difficulty of this tier. An agent that reaches T4-supported here has NOT solved the free-standing problem and the cell says so in its own text.

THE CELL BOUNDARY IS DECIDED BY THE TORQUE, NOT BY THE FORCE, AND ONLY JUST. Measured: peak applied force 5.14 N against a bound of 0.02 x m.g = 5.02 N for this 25.6 kg robot -- 1.02x over, close enough that a slightly gentler lateral gain would have fallen inside it -- while the peak applied torque is 34.22 N.m against a bound of 2 N.m, 17x over. Any rig that keeps a biped upright is decisively supported on the torque channel long before it is on the force channel, which is worth knowing before anyone reads a force figure alone. ⚠ AMENDED BY THE REPRODUCTION: the '5.02 N bound' in this bullet assumes body weight is the WHOLE ROBOT's 25.6 kg. The committed oracle reads it off the BASE BODY (12.0 kg), which makes the bound 2.3544 N and the force channel 2.36x over rather than 1.02x -- so under that reading the force channel is NOT marginal and the bullet's 'only just' is an artefact of which mass was used. The torque half stands either way and is the robust half of the finding. See T4_OPEN_QUESTION_WHICH_MASS_IS_BODY_WEIGHT.

AT 0.27 M/S THE BOB IS 0.0031 M RMS, BELOW THE 0.005 M BAR THE TIER'S TEXT STILL STATES. This run would have been red on the retired bob clause while covering 25 m with 160 footfalls and never falling -- an independent confirmation, on a two-legged robot, of the false negative the rung below measured on a four-legged one and repaired the same day. See grading_readings.T4.3_the_bob_clause_is_INHERITED_AS_RETIRED.

THE DESCRIPTION FORMAT CANNOT EXPRESS ROTOR INERTIA AND THIS ROBOT NEEDS IT. Same finding as the rung below, unchanged and not new here: with armature 0 and a stiff position servo at a 2 ms step, a light shank is numerically unstable. The demonstration set armature 0.02 kg.m^2 and damping 0.6 on the compiled model. An agent that reads the resulting bouncing as 'the robot is badly modelled' will fix the wrong thing.

THE RUN ENDED ON GEOMETRY, IN THE DEMONSTRATION ITSELF. The scratch world was 33 m of floor and the robot reached its edge margin at 24.94 m in 90 s, recorded as termination_cause: arena_geometry. The build note this tier's arena rule comes from is not hypothetical: the first world anyone builds is too small, and it happened here on the first serious run.

COLLISION IS ON THE BASE BOX AND THE TWO FOOT BOXES ONLY, so the only bodies of this robot that can ever appear in a contact are base_link, foot_l and foot_r. A column whose contact channel reports thigh or shank contacts is reporting something this description cannot produce.
authored_here.an_open_question_the_demonstration_expos: A SUPPORT RIG IMPLEMENTED AS A CONSTRAINT REPORTS NO APPLIED WRENCH. The demonstration applied its rig as an explicit body wrench, which is exactly what the applied-support channel measures. A rig implemented instead as a weld, an equality constraint, a mocap attachment or a kinematic base would hold the robot just as firmly and the wrench channel would read ZERO -- and the run would be published in T4-unsupported, which is the cell the plan says must be 'numerically nothing'. Nothing in the tier's text closes this, and nothing in this grader can: it reads what the column attests. What a column MUST do to be honest here is count constraint forces on the base as applied support, and LADDER_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE_T4 now says so in as many words. That closes the CONTRACT half and not the enforcement half: no grader can tell an omitted constraint reaction from a rig that was never there, so this stays a requirement on the column and a thing a reviewer has to check, not a thing a red row will catch. IT WAS A CONJECTURE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN. IT HAS SINCE BEEN BUILT AND RUN -- see and_it_was_DEMONSTRATED_2026_08_02 below, which confirms it exactly and is a live hole in the tier, not a theoretical one.
authored_here.and_it_was_DEMONSTRATED_2026_08_02: CONFIRMED, EXECUTED, AND CLOSED ON ONE COLUMN ONLY. The MuJoCo column built the rig the question describes -- a mocap body plus a <weld> equality binding base_link to it, with the identical scripted gait running the legs -- and graded ONE RECORDING TWICE (`python tests/benchmarks/ladder/adapters/mujoco/run_t4.py --out <dir> --rig weld`, which prints both). mjData.xfrc_applied was IDENTICALLY ZERO for the whole run, asserted rather than assumed. RESULT: (a) with the constraint reaction counted -- what LADDER_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE_T4 demands of a column -- the run is PASS 5/5 in T4-supported, published as 'supported: peak 2.188 x body weight, 94.09 N.m, 100% of window' (peak force 257.52 N, per-channel fx 254.59 / fy 15.87 / fz 93.26 N and tx 30.19 / ty 93.65 / tz 34.62 N.m, every axis live 100 % of the window); (b) with only mjData.xfrc_applied attested -- what a column that never thought about constraint rigs would publish -- THE SAME RECORDING IS PASS 5/5 IN T4-unsupported, published as 'unsupported: peak 0 x body weight, 0 N.m, 0% of window', over the same 23.3608 m of travel, WITH NO RED ASSERTION, NO VACUOUS CLAUSE, AND NOT EVEN AN excluded_from_comparison FLAG to warn a reader. A robot held rigidly upright by a constraint, covering 23 m it could not cover unaided, lands in the cell the plan reserves for numerically nothing and looks exactly like an honest unsupported walk. THE HOLE IS REAL AND IT IS NOT DETECTABLE DOWNSTREAM.
authored_here.what_the_column_side_attestation_that_cl: IMPLEMENTED ON THE MuJoCo COLUMN, 2026-08-02, in ladder/adapters/mujoco/runner_t4.py; BRINGUP_T4.md section 6 is the write-up. Two halves. (1) COUNT THE REACTION WHERE IT CAN BE COUNTED. MuJoCo assembles constraint rows in the fixed order equality, friction loss, limit, contact and publishes the first two counts as mjData.ne / mjData.nf, so the equality rows are exactly efc_J[:ne] and the generalized force they apply is efc_J[:ne].T @ efc_force[:ne]; restricted to the base's own free-joint DOFs that is a wrench about the base's centre of mass, with the translational part already in the world frame and the rotational part in the BODY frame (measured on 3.8.1, not assumed), so the torque is rotated by mjData.xmat before it is added to mjData.xfrc_applied. CONTACT ROWS ARE DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED -- T4.4 excludes contact by its own wording and counts it separately, and folding them in would publish the floor as a support rig. A tripwire test asserts the arithmetic against ground truth: a 12 kg body welded to a mocap anchor applies nothing through xfrc_applied and its equality reaction totals 117.72 N, its own weight. (2) REFUSE TO ATTEST WHERE IT CANNOT. A KINEMATIC BASE -- one welded structurally into the world's weld group -- has no degrees of freedom for a reaction to appear on, so there is no honest number; that column reports support_attestation: unverified and the run lands in T4-support-unverified, excluded from comparison and never credited. T4-unsupported means 'nothing was applied'; T4-support-unverified means 'nobody knows'; a held robot belongs in the second and never in the first. The same refusal fires if an actuator acts on the base's free joint or the scene carries tendons, because the total would then be partial. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO is close the question on any other column: the grader reads what a column attests and an omitted constraint reaction is indistinguishable from a rig that was never there. What it adds is a worked demonstration that the requirement BITES, with both cells printed, so a reviewer checking another column knows exactly what to ask for and what a failure to supply it looks like.
authored_here.T4_OPEN_QUESTION_WHICH_MASS_IS_BODY_WEIG: FOUND BY THE REPRODUCTION, MEASURED, NOT FIXED, AND IT MOVES THE CELL BOUNDARY BY A FACTOR OF 2.13 ON THIS ROBOT. The tier publishes the peak support force as 'a multiple of body weight' and sets the unsupported cell at 0.02 x m.g, and the grader takes that m from the base_mass channel. On a humanoid there are two defensible answers and the shipped description makes them far apart: the BASE BODY's own mass (12.0 kg -- base_link is pelvis and trunk) and the WHOLE ROBOT's (25.6 kg). The same unchanged run therefore reads 'peak 0.04715 x body weight against a 2.3544 N bound' under the first and 'peak 0.02210 x body weight against a 5.0228 N bound' under the second. THE SCRATCH DEMONSTRATION USED THE SECOND (it attested sum(body_mass[1:]) as the base's mass) AND THE COMMITTED ORACLE USES THE FIRST (mjModel.body_mass[base_link]), which is the literal reading of 'the base's mass', is what the tier below already reports, and is the STRICTER of the two -- and that difference, not any physical one, is most of the apparent 2.3x gap between the two records' support figures (the actual peak forces are 5.14 N and 5.55 N). The MuJoCo column records the subtree mass beside the base mass and writes the whole ambiguity into the channel's own citation so it travels into every verdict. WHICH ONE THE TIER MEANS IS FOR ITS OWNER TO SETTLE BEFORE THE FREEZE, and the number was not chosen after seeing a measurement: deciding it that way is the act section 5a voids a pass for. Note that the tier below is unaffected in practice only because nobody has looked -- its base is 6.0 kg of a lighter robot and the same question applies to it verbatim.
what_a_demonstration_must_produce: A run of THIS description, unmodified, built into a scene by one column's own documented path, graded PASS 5/5 through the real ladder.graders.t4_core with NO vacuous clause and NO unanswered channel.

Its cell named -- T4-unsupported or T4-supported -- and if supported, the peak force as a multiple of body weight, the peak applied torque and the fraction of the window support was live, printed with it.
The world it ran in offering the run-up ARENA.txt states, with the extent attested so the grader can say so.

A committed oracle in the shape T1 and T2 already have -- a runner plus a bring-up note carrying the recipe, the verbatim verdict and the effort ledger -- reproducing it with one command. A demonstration run from an uncommitted scratch harness is a claim a reader cannot re-derive, which the standing 'no row, no result' rule (agent-edge-validation-plan.md section 0.2) does not accept.
authored_here.all_four_of_those_are_now_SATISFIED_on_o: 2026-08-02, MuJoCo. (2) Its cell named and its three figures printed inside it: T4-supported, 'peak 0.04715 x body weight, 50.2 N.m, 100% of window'. (3) The world attested: a bounded 150 m x 12 m slab offering 145.123 m of straight run from the start against the 15.0 m ARENA.txt states, arena_attestation attested, and the length is DERIVED from this file's own 300 s window times the gait's own speed rather than chosen -- a shorter floor ends the run by the robot walking off the edge, which the fall test reads as a FALL and not as an arena finding. (4) The committed oracle: `python tests/benchmarks/ladder/adapters/mujoco/run_t4.py --out <dir>`, with BRINGUP_T4.md carrying the recipe, both verbatim verdicts, every trap and the effort ledger. NONE OF THIS IS A LADDER CELL and none of it is a claim about any agent, any other column, or the unsupported cell.
authored_here.the_demonstration_IS_a_committed_oracle: YES, since 2026-08-02: adapters/mujoco/run_t4.py (with t4_scene/t4_drive/runner_t4 and BRINGUP_T4.md) reproduces both cells from the repository -- supported PASS 5/5 at 73.30 m, and --rig none FAIL 2/5 falling at 0.69 m. The scratch script it replaced is superseded; its 13.2% higher distance came from two defects reported rather than reproduced (a hip-IK sign that walks this robot backwards, and an ankle offset that drops the foot box's own origin). Prior status, kept: ⚠ THIS KEY'S NAME IS NOW FALSE AND THE KEY IS KEPT ANYWAY, deliberately: ladder/graders/test_t4_core.py asserts it BY NAME, and the grader is not this work's to edit. IT IS NOW A COMMITTED ORACLE -- the substantive entry is the_demonstratio

robot.note: The name of the ROOT LINK of the shipped description, which is the body T4 measures: every threshold in the tier is about the base. The grader prefers the body carrying this name and refuses -- loudly, with the sentence in the row -- rather than grading the luckiest of several. The description's <robot name> is 'strider'; a column whose converter names the base body after the robot rather than after the link will not match, which is the open question below.
robot.standing_geometry: ⚠ TWO OF THE THREE NUMBERS IN THIS BLOCK ARE WRONG AND ARE LEFT VISIBLE ON PURPOSE -- see container.authored_here.and_this_file_s_own_standing_geometry_carries_the_same_20_mm_ERROR for the measured values and why the wrong ones are still here. With every joint at zero the legs are straight and the sole sits 0.725 m below the base origin [CORRECT: the compiled model returns 0.7250 m]. With a crouch of hip pitch 0.30, knee -0.60, ankle pitch 0.30 the sole sits 0.680 m below it and each foot is still directly under its own hip [WRONG: 0.7000 m -- the 0.680 assumes an ankle-to-sole distance of 0.04 m and the real one is 0.06 m]. Each leg reaches between 0.09 m and 0.60 m from the hip pitch axis to the sole [WRONG: 0.2888 .. 0.6198 m; the upper end carries the same 0.04 m error and the lower end matches nothing this knee can do]. The knee's upper limit is -0.05 rad rather than 0 because a knee allowed to lock straight sits on the singularity of every two-link leg solution [CORRECT, and the reproduction confirms the substance: the knee limit and not the reach is what binds].
robot.open_question_for_the_freeze: A converter that names the base body after the robot ('strider') rather than after the root link ('base_link'), or that prefixes or namespaces link names, produces bodies that carry neither name, and the grader then refuses the cell rather than grading the wrong body. Whether the task should carry an alias list, and who decides an alias is legitimate, is undecided -- it is the same open question T2's roles block and T3's robot block record.

ground.resolution_rule: A contact counts as a contact with the ground only when the other body's name is one of these AND the column's own channel attests that it is the ground. Every disagreement between the two is printed in the row and resolved towards the STRICTER reading in both directions.
ground.why_not_in_the_container: Which bodies are the ground is task data, for the reason T1's waypoint and T2's roles are, and with more at stake than either: T4.4 asserts that NOTHING BUT THE GROUND touched the robot, so an adapter free to decide what counts as the ground could label the thing holding the robot up as the floor and pass the assertion outright.
ground.open_question_for_the_freeze: A scene whose ground the agent named something outside this list produces FOREIGN contacts on every footfall and a false red on T4.4. The row names the offending body and prints the adapter/task disagreement, so the misread is diagnosable in one glance rather than silent -- but it is still a red for a naming reason. Whether the name list should be replaced by a geometric rule (the static body the feet rested on during the settle window) is undecided. The list is deliberately generous and is the same list the tier below uses.

arena.rule: MIN_RUN_UP_FACTOR x NET_DISPLACEMENT_M. The deliverable's world must offer at least this much straight run from where the robot starts, and the requirement is SHIPPED TO THE AGENT in container/ARENA.txt.
arena.why: docs/developer/g1-endurance-2026-08-01.md section 8, from six measured runs of this tree's own flagship on a weight-bearing balance harness: 'The world, not the policy, ended every single run ... all six runs here would have been misread as the walk degrades to 0.037 m/s after ~110 s by a grader that did not know where the walls were.' The shipped arena there caps travel at 12.9 m, i.e. 29 % above a 10 m bar, and fails a 15 m rule outright. capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4 turns that measurement into a binding build note for every column.
arena.what_the_grader_does_with_it: Three things, none of them a pass condition. (1) It records the longest straight run the region allowed from the run's own start, beside this requirement, in every verdict. (2) When the region is smaller than the BAR, T4.1's 'crossed ten metres' clause reports its witness ABSENT -- the assertion could not have passed, which is a statement about the world the deliverable built and not about the gait. (3) When the base has been within ARENA_MARGIN_M of the region's edge for the last PLATEAU_WINDOW_S of the recording, the run is recorded as termination: arena_geometry and the scored window ENDS there, so the speed, the bob and the footfall count are measured over the walk rather than over the stretch spent at the wall.
arena.the_guard_on_that_last_one: Truncating a window could hide a gait that degraded, so it only happens when the column POSITIVELY attests where the region ends AND the base is demonstrably at that edge. A plateau in open floor is a STALL, is named one, and is scored in full. The whole-recording mean speed is printed beside the scored one in every row, labelled as not being the walking speed.
arena.how_this_tier_differs_from_the_one_below: See grading_readings.T4_arena_bound_does_not_require_a_stop. The rule one rung down asks whether the base STOPPED at the edge; this one does not, because the run it exists for was still moving.
arena.absent_arena_is_an_INCOMPLETE_cell: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4, build note 1: 'a T4 cell whose recorder cannot see it is support_attestation-style incomplete rather than quietly graded.' Implemented as arena_attestation: unverified plus an entry in comparison_exclusions and excluded_from_comparison: true. See grading_readings.T4_an_unattested_arena_excludes_the_cell_from_comparison -- it is an EXTENSION of the plan's text, declared for a reviewer to attack.

harness.why: T4 is graded entirely from the standalone cold re-run. A live session observing the agent's own scene answers nothing T4 asks that the re-run does not answer better -- and a walk that only happens while the agent is holding it up is exactly what phase B exists to catch.

standalone.note: Phase B, per SPEC 2.3: the deliverable is re-run cold, standalone, with the grader's own sampler injected and no agent present. duration_s must fit ten metres at the tier's own speed floor -- 10.0 / 0.15 = 66.7 s -- AND leave room for a walker slower than the floor to be MEASURED as slow rather than truncated. The only long humanoid walk this tree has measured takes 82.9 s to reach the bar, so a 180 s window would have measured it with little to spare; 300 s is four and a half times the arithmetic minimum and about three and a half times that measured artifact.
standalone.settle_note: 1.5 s rather than the 1.0 s one rung down. A two-legged robot dropped into a scene needs longer to settle onto two feet than a four-legged one does onto four, and the settled standing height read at t=0 is the datum the whole fall test is stated against.
standalone.contact_stride_note: The contact query must run often enough to resolve a footfall: a two-legged gait cycle is order 1 s and a stride of 2 basic steps samples it many times over. The times the query ran are part of the channel -- a list of touches carries no evidence of a LIFTED foot, and a channel that omits them makes the transition clause report itself vacuous rather than counting zero and calling the robot a slider.
standalone.surfaces_note: Despite the name this is the list of non-robot bodies the grader asks the sampler to BOUND at t=0 and to classify in contacts. It is the same list as ground.names on purpose: the walking region's extent is derived from the union of their world boxes, which is what makes an arena-bound run distinguishable from a stall. Names the agent chose differently are simply not bounded; the affected measurements then report their witnesses absent, and the blocker is ours.

constants_note: EVERY ONE OF THESE IS THE TIER-BELOW MODULE'S OWN GLOBAL, IMPORTED AND NOT RESTATED. capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4 says 'T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T3.5 unchanged', and t4_core implements that by CALLING those row builders -- which read their own module's globals. A copy of a number in t4_core would therefore be a number that looks binding and is not, so t4_core imports them and re-exports the names, and the test compares this file against t4_core in both directions. The first eight are capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T3's numbers as adopted by section 2 T4 (and the last two of the eight are section 2 T4's own two-cell boundary, which states the same 0.02 x m.g and 2 N.m); the last six are witness bounds, one derived clause and the arena rule the tier's wording implies rather than states. The BAR STAYS AT 10.0 M: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4 pre-registered it, measured our own artifact against it afterwards, and kept it verbatim because a threshold that moves after the measurement is worthless whichever way it moves.

support.the_decision: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4: 'The task PERMITS a support harness, and every cell measures the support instead of asserting its absence.' Forbidding it would make this tier a task we already know we fail, which is uninformative in the opposite direction from rigging; and 'harnessed / unharnessed' hides the difference between a fingertip and a crane. So the wrench is measured, in newtons and newton-metres, and published.

the_two_cells.T4-unsupported: peak non-gravitational, non-contact force on the base <= MAX_SUPPORT_FORCE_FRACTION x m.g AND <= MAX_SUPPORT_TORQUE_NM -- numerically nothing.
the_two_cells.T4-supported: anything larger, published WITH the measured peak force as a multiple of body weight, the peak applied torque in N.m, and the fraction of the walk window during which support was non-zero, printed INSIDE the cell.
the_two_cells.T4-support-unverified: NOT ONE OF THE PLAN'S TWO CELLS, and named differently so it can never be counted as one. It is where a column that cannot attest the applied wrench lands: recorded, excluded from comparison with any cell that has a total, never failed and never credited.

support.two_cells_from_ONE_recording: Both cells come from the same run. The grader does not run the deliverable twice and does not ask the agent which cell it is aiming at: it records the wrench, and the wrench selects the cell. A supported run is NOT a failure of the tier -- it is a different cell -- and section 8 forbids quoting either without its figures.
support.the_wrench_never_fails_the_row: See grading_readings.T4.4_the_wrench_routes_the_cell_and_never_fails_the_row. What CAN fail T4.4 is the contact half: a robot leaning on a wall, propped on a crate, dragged along a rail or held by another body. Negative fixture: leaning_on_scene_geometry.

measured_per_channel.the_requirement: Peak and fraction-non-zero are recorded PER AXIS for force and for torque, not as a single magnitude.
measured_per_channel.why: docs/developer/g1-endurance-2026-08-01.md section 4, measured over a whole 10 m walk on this tree's own rig at body weight 334.5 N: the VERTICAL CARRYING CHANNEL READ 0.00 N AND WAS LIVE 0 % OF THE WINDOW while the ATTITUDE CHANNEL PEAKED AT 69.2 N.m AND WAS LIVE 100 % OF IT, with a 36.8 N lateral catch (0.110 x body weight). One scalar reports that rig as 'peak 36.8 N, non-zero 100 % of the window' and hides the entire finding: a reader cannot tell a rig that CARRIES a robot from one that only keeps it from TOPPLING, and those are different claims about what the robot did.
measured_per_channel.a_column_that_can_only_summarise: Still counts as attested and still lands in a real cell. Its row reports the per-channel clause VACUOUS and a note says the cell cannot say which channel held the robot up. Negative fixture: summarised_support.
measured_per_channel.and_what_it_does_not_prove: That the flagship walk is nearly free-standing. The endurance document is explicit and this file repeats it: the attitude spring is 600 N.m/rad with a +/- 350 N.m capacity, and the fact that the pelvis never sank below the rig's target height is plausibly A CONSEQUENCE OF that spring holding it up. The measurement narrows the claim; it does not remove the harness.

support.measured_over_the_scored_window: The published fraction is 'of the walk window', so the profile the row grades and the cell publishes is restricted to the scored window. The tier below measures its wrench half over whatever window the column attested, because there a wrench outside the walk is still a wrench somebody applied; here the number has a stated denominator and it is the walk. Where the column's wrench log carries no clock the window cannot be applied and the profile says so (window_applied: false) rather than pretending.
support.attested_requires_two_things: the column positively attests the applied wrench AND the base's mass and the world's gravity are known -- because the cell boundary is 0.02 x m.g and the published figure is a multiple of body weight. Either missing makes the run T4-support-unverified.
support.section_9_Q2: capability-ladder-plan.md section 9 Q2 records this channel as the largest new build in the programme and asks whether it exists on any column but ours. It does exist on ours and it is per-axis and per-tick (g1-endurance-2026-08-01.md section 4 prints fx/fy/fz/tx/ty/tz for a whole walk). If most columns can only answer unverified, this tier's grid will be one in which our column is the only one whose support is comparable at all -- which is a reason to find reviewers, not a reason to relax the measurement.

termination_fields.distance_to_termination_m: the net horizontal base displacement actually reached, whatever it was, NOT clipped at the bar.
termination_fields.where_they_come_from: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4 and section 3.2 state both fields, with exactly this vocabulary, FOR THIS TIER. They are required in every T4 cell, passing or failing, on every column.
termination_fields.why_they_exist: so that a 10.1 m run and a 29.5 m run are distinguishable in the published grid, and so that a run which stopped because it ran out of floor is never read as one that degraded -- which is exactly how six clean measured runs of this tree's own flagship would have been misread. Neither is a pass condition and neither may be turned into one: the bar stays at 10.0 m exactly as pre-registered, and section 2 T4 records the resulting weakness (10 m sits at about a third of that artifact's demonstrated reach, so this tier is less discriminating than it looks) rather than fixing it after the fact.
termination_fields.recorded_where: every verdict's measurements, including the ones that fail before any physics is read (where the distance is null and the cause is 'unknown' -- 'the field was missing' and 'the run ended at the clock' are different statements).
termination_fields.section_8: capability-ladder-plan.md section 8 forbids quoting a T4 cell without its termination_cause, and forbids describing a run that ran out of floor as a walk that degraded, a stall, or a fall.

method.why_not: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T3, inherited by section 2 T4: 'Training is permitted. GPU-hours are a cost field, not a disqualification; a cell that reaches the outcome by training a policy and a cell that reaches it by a model-based gait are both achieved, with method recorded.' The tier is a physical outcome and the route to it is a fact readers want, never a pass condition.
method.asserted_mechanically: test_t4_core grades one run under all four values and requires byte-identical assertions -- because 'we promise not to grade it' is a comment, and that is a test.

reuse_class.decided_by: a human reviewer, never the grader.
reuse_class.why_the_grader_leaves_it_null: capability-ladder-plan.md section 9 Q3 records that the boundary is fuzzy -- 'an agent that edits three env vars in a shipped recipe is what?' -- and that the reviewer arbitrates. It asks whether the deliverable's BEHAVIOUR would exist without work done during the run, which is a judgement about the session and not a measurement of it. Every T4 verdict therefore carries the field, carries it as null, and carries a note saying a cell published with it still null is not publishable.
reuse_class.why_it_matters_most_on_THIS_tier: section 8 forbids quoting a T3 or T4 cell without it, and on this tier the gap between the two labels is at its widest: 'an agent composed a shipped humanoid walking skill' and 'an agent made a humanoid walk' are separated by human-years, and the grid must never let them merge.

expectation.T4-unsupported: not_achieved -- a stated cross in our own column, pre-registered before any cell ran
expectation.T4-supported: achieved, reuse_class: assembled -- capability-ladder-plan.md section 6.4's pre-registration, revised 2026-08-02 after the distance was measured. THIS FILE DOES NOT CHANGE IT.
expectation.reasoning: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4 and the expectation table in section 6.4. The unsupported cell is not_achieved(no_physics_capability -> open research) by this tree's own canonical RL status: a durable free-standing humanoid walk is an open problem here and no G1 walk champion has ever been shown at lambda = 0. The supported cell was expected to fail on DISTANCE until section 9 Q1 forced the measurement, and the measurement refuted the expectation: 10.0 m at t = 82.9 s, 6 of 6 runs, zero falls, 29.5 m in a longer arena -- ALL ON THE lambda = 0.9 WEIGHT-BEARING BALANCE HARNESS, which no sentence about it may omit.
expectation.the_prior_pre_registration_kept_visible: 'uncertain, leaning not_achieved on distance -- flagship measures 0.120 m/s; 10 m is about 83 s of continuous walking, longer than any G1 bout recorded in this tree.' That expectation was refuted by measurement; the 10.0 m bar it was written against did not move.
expectation.what_this_file_adds_without_changing_the: A measurement the revision did not consider: at 0.1207 m/s made good, the flagship is BELOW this tier's inherited 0.15 m/s speed floor, so on the clause rather than on the distance our own supported cell would read not_achieved today. That is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION for whoever owns the tier (grading_readings.T4.3_OPEN_QUESTION_our_own_flagship_is_below_the_speed_floor) and NOT as a revised expectation, because revising an expectation after seeing a number is the same act as moving a threshold after seeing a number.
expectation.the_trap_that_has_already_voided_a_legge: If the model runtime is missing from the interpreter that spawns controllers -- a different interpreter from the one the engine embeds -- the deploy runs a ZERO-RESIDUAL BARE-GHOST BASELINE AND EXITS 0. Assert the load line, never the exit code. T4.5 encodes exactly this (inherited from T3.5), and the negative fixture is policy_never_loaded.
expectation.pre_registered: capability-ladder-plan.md section 6.4 -- written before any cell runs, printed beside the outcome in the published report.

cost_class: GPU, and capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4 calls it the highest engineering cost in the ladder. A column that reaches this rung by training pays for the training; a column that reaches it with a hand-written gait pays in engineering instead, and the method field records which. capability-ladder-plan.md section 6 sequences T4 as step 5, behind the owner's per-campaign cloud approval.

grading_readings.T4_rows_1_2_3_and_5_are_the_other_tier_s: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T4: 'T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T3.5 unchanged. T3.4 is REPLACED by the support measurement.' t4_core implements 'unchanged' as THE SAME FUNCTION: it calls the tier-below core's own row builders and relabels the assertion id. If one of those rows is ever corrected, this tier inherits the correction instead of drifting away from it, which is what the word has to mean to be worth writing down. test_t4_core asserts it mechanically -- it grades one run through both cores and requires the four reused rows to come out field for field identical, id excepted. Everything those rows read -- their thresholds, their readings about furthest-not-final distance, yaw-discarding roll and pitch, speed made good, the detrended bob, per-body contact transitions -- is documented in T3_quadruped/meta.json and is not restated here, because a second copy of a reading is a second reading.
grading_readings.T4.4_the_contact_half_survives_and_that_: DECLARED, NOT TRANSCRIBED. Section 2 T4 says T3.4 is 'replaced by the support measurement below', and the two-cell table that follows is stated purely in force and torque units. Read strictly, T3.4's FIRST half -- 'no contact with any body other than the ground' -- would vanish, and a humanoid propped against scene geometry or dragged along a rail would land in T4-unsupported, the cell the plan says must be 'numerically nothing'. No applied-wrench channel can see a physical prop. So the contact half is kept: it costs no column anything (it is the clause it already had one rung down), and it is what stops the unsupported cell from being reachable by a robot that was held. A reviewer who thinks the replacement was meant to be total should say so before the freeze. Negative fixture: leaning_on_scene_geometry, which applies ZERO force and is still red.
grading_readings.T4.4_the_wrench_routes_the_cell_and_neve: The single most consequential reading in this tier, and it is the plan's rather than an inference: section 2 T4 permits a support rig, publishes two cells, and prints a SUPPORTED cell as 'achieved'. So an applied wrench above the unsupported bounds moves the run to the other cell and does not redden anything. The obvious objection -- that a robot carried outright would then pass -- is answered by the other rows and deliberately: T4.3 requires a gait (a bob about the trend AND make-and-break ground contact), T4.1 requires continuity, and the cell PRINTS THE NUMBER. Negative-control fixture: carried_outright, which passes under 2.09 x body weight and 348 N.m for 100 % of the window and publishes exactly that string. There is no upper bound on support, by design -- see T4_OPEN_QUESTION_a_supported_cell_has_no_ceiling.
grading_readings.T4.4_is_measured_over_the_scored_window: See support.measured_over_the_scored_window. A contact after the walk has ended -- the robot resting against whatever stopped it -- is an ARENA finding, not a support finding, and does not redden the clause; it is counted and printed separately. An UNTIMED foreign contact is counted as inside, which is the strict direction: an adapter that cannot say when something touched the robot does not get the benefit of the doubt. That half is inherited unchanged from the tier below.
grading_readings.T4.4_per_channel_or_the_cell_cannot_say_: See support.measured_per_channel. Per-axis peaks and per-axis fractions, or the clause reports itself vacuous.
grading_readings.T4.4_unverified_is_NEITHER_cell: Section 2 T4: 'Where a simulator cannot attest applied forces, the cell is achieved (support unverified) and is excluded from comparison with an attested cell.' Implemented as a PASS with the wrench clauses vacuous, cell: T4-support-unverified, and excluded_from_comparison: true. Failing it would publish OUR missing channel as somebody else's capability gap, which section 4's binding rule forbids; passing it silently is what section 5c exists to prevent. Negative fixture: support_not_attested.
grading_readings.T4_arena_bound_does_not_require_a_stop: THIS TIER STRENGTHENS THE RULE ONE RUNG BELOW, and the reason is measured rather than theoretical. The rule below declares a run arena-bound only when the base STOPPED at the region's edge. docs/developer/g1-endurance-2026-08-01.md section 4 records what actually happened to the only long humanoid walk this tree has: x froze against a wall at 12.90 m while y ran out to -6.88 m over two hundred seconds -- the robot was pressed against the world and STILL LOCOMOTING, so a rule keyed on 'it stopped' can miss it entirely and the run reads as a gait that degraded. t4_core.arena_bound_index asks only that the base has been within ARENA_MARGIN_M of the edge for the last PLATEAU_WINDOW_S of the recording, moving or not. The guard is unchanged and is the conjunction itself: the column must POSITIVELY attest where the region ends, and a plateau in open floor is a stall, is named one, and is scored in full. Negative fixtures: arena_bound (it stopped) and arena_bound_still_moving (it did not), and test_t4_core asserts that the rule below returns None on the second series while this one does not.
grading_readings.T4_an_unattested_arena_excludes_the_cell: AN EXTENSION OF THE PLAN'S TEXT, DECLARED RATHER THAN SMUGGLED. Section 2 T4 build note 1 says a T4 cell whose recorder cannot see arena contact is 'support_attestation-style incomplete rather than quietly graded'. The plan states the CONSEQUENCE of the support-attestation rule -- exclusion from comparison -- for support only, so applying it to the arena is an inference from 'support_attestation-style'. It is implemented as arena_attestation: unverified plus a named entry in comparison_exclusions plus excluded_from_comparison: true, and the assertions are untouched. A reviewer who thinks an unattested arena should merely be annotated rather than excluded should say so before the freeze. Fixture: no_arena_channel, which PASSES and is flagged.
grading_readings.T4.3_OPEN_QUESTION_our_own_flagship_is_b: OPEN AT THE FREEZE, MEASURED, NOT FIXED, AND THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL THING IN THIS FILE. This tier inherits T3.3's mean-speed floor of 0.15 m/s unchanged. docs/developer/g1-endurance-2026-08-01.md measures the shipped flagship crossing 10.0 m at t = 82.88 s in six of six runs with zero falls, which is 0.1207 m/s made good -- RED against that floor. So the artifact whose DISTANCE was measured before the freeze, and which caused section 6.4's expectation for T4-supported to be revised from not_achieved to achieved, would fail this tier on SPEED. (All of it on the lambda = 0.9 weight-bearing balance harness, which no sentence about it may omit.) NO THRESHOLD WAS MOVED and none should be: 0.15 m/s is the plan's number by way of T3.3, and moving it after seeing a measurement is exactly what section 5a voids a pass for and what section 9 Q1 forbids in the analogous case. What is recorded instead is the question, for whoever owns the tier: is a speed floor inherited from a four-legged tier the floor that was meant for a two-legged one? A quadruped trot and a humanoid walk are not the same physical problem, and 0.15 m/s is a brisk quadruped and a slow human. It is executable as the fixture flagship_measured_speed, whose numbers are the measured ones.
grading_readings.T4.3_the_bob_clause_is_INHERITED_AS_RETI: INHERITED DIVERGENCE, NOT A CHOICE MADE HERE. On 2026-08-02 the rung below RETIRED the 0.005 m RMS vertical-oscillation clause: it is still computed, still printed in every row beside the bar it used to apply, and NEVER GRADED, because it was demonstrated failing a robot that was plainly walking. This tier calls that row rather than copying it, so it inherits the retirement automatically -- which is the whole point of implementing 'unchanged' as 'the same function'. THIS TIER'S OWN DEMONSTRATION CONFIRMS THE DEFECT ON A TWO-LEGGED ROBOT: the scripted walk above covers 24.94 m at 0.2699 m/s with 160 footfalls and never falls, and bobs 0.0031 m RMS -- red against a bar that is no longer applied. WHAT REMAINS OPEN is a text divergence, not a behaviour: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T3 (and section 2 T4 by inheritance) still STATES the >= 0.005 m clause, and the graders no longer apply it. The tier owner has to reconcile the plan's text with the code before the freeze; the code is what runs, and it is declared here rather than left to be discovered in a diff.
grading_readings.T4_OPEN_QUESTION_a_supported_cell_has_no: OPEN AT THE FREEZE, DELIBERATE, NOT FIXED. Nothing bounds how much support a T4-supported cell may carry: a robot held at 2.09 x its body weight for 100 % of the window is published as achieved with those figures. That is the plan's own worked example and it follows from 'a supported run is a different cell, not a failure'. The honest consequence is that T4-supported can be reached by a rig doing most of the work, and what contains it is disclosure rather than a threshold: the number is inside the cell and section 8 forbids quoting the cell without it. Whether the tier should ALSO carry a stated band (say, a separate label above 1.0 x body weight) is undecided, and adding one after a cell runs would be a tier change rather than a bug fix.
grading_readings.T4_OPEN_QUESTION_no_clause_reads_the_ter: OPEN AT THE FREEZE, INHERITED, NOT FIXED. The tier says 'flat ground' and not one assertion checks that the ground was flat -- a deliverable that builds a downhill slope would be graded identically, and gravity would do part of the work. On a two-legged robot that matters more than on a four-legged one. The evidence to close it exists (the walking surface's world box is already read for the arena), but 'the ground is level to within X' is a SIXTH pass condition the plan's table does not state, and adding one before the freeze is a tier change rather than a bug fix.
grading_readings.T4_OPEN_QUESTION_a_run_that_walks_and_th: OPEN AT THE FREEZE, INHERITED, NOT FIXED. Because the scored window ends where the bar is reached, a robot that crosses ten metres cleanly and then collapses at metre eleven fails T4.2 -- which reads every recorded sample -- but keeps a clean T4.3. A T4 cell therefore says nothing about durability beyond the bar. The plan does not ask it to; section 7's 'achieved does not mean reliable' applies here with particular force at n = 3, and with more force still on an artifact whose three runs are reproducibility checks rather than independent samples (g1-endurance-2026-08-01.md section 6).

disclosure.the_rule: AGENTS.md's humanoid disclosure rule: never describe a harnessed humanoid walk as free-standing. Every G1 result in this tree runs on a weight-bearing balance rig -- lambda = 0.9, up to about 2x body weight of vertical capacity and +/- 350 N.m of attitude authority -- and a durable free-standing humanoid walk is an OPEN problem here.
disclosure.what_the_grader_can_and_cannot_do_about_: It cannot enforce prose. What it does instead is make the number impossible to lose: the support figures are written into EVERY verdict including the ones that fail before any physics is read, the cell name carries the word, and measurements.cell_text renders the exact parenthetical a cell must be published with. A tool that prints a T4 cell without those figures is printing something this grader did not produce.
disclosure.and_the_measurement_narrows_rather_than_: On the one walk this tree has measured per channel, the vertical carrying channel was idle. That narrows the honest claim -- the rig's CAPACITY is about 2x body weight, its USE on that run was 0 N vertical plus up to 69.2 N.m of attitude authority and a 0.11 x body-weight lateral catch -- and it does not make the walk free-standing, because the attitude spring ran continuously and the pelvis's never sinking is plausibly a consequence of it.

negative_fixtures.rule: capability-ladder-plan.md section 5c.2: no assertion enters a ladder cell until it has been observed FAILING on a deliberately wrong artifact. Each fixture is the oracle with ONE thing wrong and must redden its own assertion AND NO OTHER, leave exactly the declared clauses vacuous, AND land in the declared cell -- a null agent turning everything red does not satisfy the rule.
negative_fixtures.the_cell_is_part_of_the_map: Every fixture declares which of the three cells it must publish in, and the check is exact. All three are reachable by some fixture, which is what makes the two-cell mechanism itself falsifiable rather than merely implemented.
